daily_baselines.py.verdict: BROKEN — the guard rails hold but the numbers do not. 63 mutants run against the selftest (41 killed, 21 survived). The refusal/omission machinery is genuinely well-tested, but (a) NOT ONE Brier or log-loss value is pinned anywhere, so the module's entire quantitative output is unverified; (b) the central 8/3 cross-book prohibition is bypassable live through at least three reachable shapes, each producing a number and a gate-PASS; (c) gate() returns green on a zero-game report and on a one-game report that prints a definitive "the cohort demonstrated nothing" verdict; (d) format_report() crashes on a report gate() calls valid. Nine claimed fixtures are decorative. READS-ONLY, the strictly-before prior rule, and the same-games/omission gate rules are the parts that survive adversarial pressure intact.

defects.issue: No Brier or log-loss value is pinned by any fixture — the module's entire scoring arithmetic is untested and both functions can be silently wrong while the selftest reports PASS and gate() reports green.
defects.evidence: Mutant `brier(): return (p-y)**2 -> return abs(p-y)` (line 89) SURVIVES: selftest exits 0, v2 cohort Brier is reported as 0.466667 instead of 0.226667, gate()==True. Mutant `logloss(): return -(...) -> return (...)` (line 93) SURVIVES: selftest exits 0, v2 log loss is reported as -0.645981 (a NEGATIVE log loss printed to the operator), gate()==True. Grepping the whole selftest for brier/logloss assertions returns only `is not None` checks, one cross-block `!=` inequality, and one value check `want = round(sum(brier(...))/5, 6)` — which calls the module's OWN brier(), so it moves with the mutation and can never detect it. Zero literal Brier/log-loss constants appear in the file.
defects.fix: Pin at least one absolute value per scorer against a hand-computed constant that does not call the module: assert score_probs on a two-game fixture gives brier == 0.2 and logloss == 0.5 to 6dp (e.g. p=.6/y=1 and p=.4/y=0 -> brier 0.16, logloss 0.510826), and assert logloss(EPS_clamped) is finite and POSITIVE. Also assert brier(0.6,1) == 0.16 and logloss(0.6,1) == 0.510826 directly.

defects.issue: gate() returns green on a report with zero common games, and there is no minimum-sample guard at any size — a one-game slate prints a definitive 'the cohort demonstrated nothing' verdict in the same imperative voice as the 15-game finding the module was written for.
defects.evidence: D.baselines('2026-08-21', [], res_rows, None) -> n_games_common=0, gate() == (True, []). Two cohorts with disjoint game sets (v1 on A@B, v2 on C@D) — precisely the 'not a head-to-head' condition the module exists to detect — also gives n_games_common=0, gate() == (True, []). Worse, the real run `python3 harness/daily_baselines.py --date 2026-08-21` (the module's own motivating slate) resolves to 1 common game and EXITS 0, printing: 'ALWAYS_HOME 1-0 (1.0000) BEAT the best cohort v1 0-1 (0.0000) on this slate. The cohort demonstrated nothing here — a blind home-side rule scored better. Report this comparison; do not lead with a cohort-versus-cohort improvement.' That is a single coin flip rendered as an actionable directive, with nothing in the output or the gate marking it as non-inferential.
defects.fix: Add a gate rule: n_games_common == 0 is a blocking failure (no comparison exists), and n below a stated floor (e.g. 5) marks the headline verdict as null with reason SAMPLE_TOO_SMALL_FOR_A_VERDICT rather than emitting BEAT/did-not-beat prose. Have _headline() suppress the 'demonstrated nothing' consequence sentence below that floor.

starter_attribution.py.verdict: NOT SOUND AS CLAIMED. The 29 claimed mutants are real — I reproduced every one against a mirrored copy and all 29 die. But the mutant set was drawn from the fixture list, not from the rule list, and five of the eleven claimed rules have NO fixture at all. I injected 60 mutants; 20 survived a fully green selftest, including a look-ahead mutant that feeds the slate's own finals into `form`, a mutant that guts the transcription-fidelity gate, and a mutant that rounds arm probabilities to 2 dp. Separately there is a live reporting defect on registered data: a game with NEITHER slot treated reports `joint = +0.0000` — a structural zero rendered as a measurement, carrying a render-gate-blessed "keyed-seed reference starter effect +0.00 points" label — and that zero is averaged into the slate `joint_pp` mean. This occurs on 4 of the 10 registered v2/v3 cards in the repo, including 2026-08-19 ATH@KC. The module's own R1 doctrine forbids exactly this for `away_only`/`home_only` and simply omits `joint`. Also, the one uncertainty number the module prints (`mc_se_pp_unpaired`) is documented as an upper bound on the paired delta's SE and measurably is not one for the module's own headline game.

defects.issue: `joint` is reported as a numeric 0.0 when NEITHER slot is treated — a structural zero presented as a measurement, in direct violation of the module's own R1 doctrine, and it is then averaged into the slate joint_pp mean. It also acquires a causal, render-gate-passing label.

When both v2 slots are CAP, _arms() builds arm (d) == arm (a) element-for-element and CRN makes them bit-identical, so joint is exactly 0.0 for a mechanical reason.

Real registered data, not synthetic — `python3 harness/starter_attribution.py --date 2026-08-19 --v1 cards/2026-08-19_card.json --v2 cards/2026-08-19_card_v2.json --n 4000`:

defects.issue: `mc_se_pp_unpaired` is the only uncertainty number the module prints, its docstring calls it an upper bound on the paired delta's SE, and it measurably is not one for the module's own headline game. The function also has no fixture whatsoever — inverting the formula survives.
defects.evidence:
Docstring of _mc_se_pp: 'An UNPAIRED bound: the paired delta's SE is smaller.' For Var(delta)=2V(1-rho) to be <= V requires rho >= 0.5, and the module's own text argues CRN pairing here is only PARTIAL because gamma/poisson are rejection samplers.

Measured, 300 keyed replicates at n=4000 using the registered 2026-08-21 ATL@MIL stat vectors (Sale k=29.8 away, Misiorowski k=39.6 home, pf 0.973 — the first row of the real slate):
    corr(arm a, arm d) = +0.4759
    sd(one arm)        = 0.8533 pp
    sd(joint delta)    = 0.8993 pp      ratio 1.054  -> the 'bound' is EXCEEDED
    home-real-only arm : corr +0.4489, sd(delta) 0.8650, ratio 1.014 -> also exceeded
(A mild treatment does satisfy it — CAP-vs-ACE gives rho 0.68, ratio 0.813 — so the claim holds only when the treatment is small, i.e. when the delta does not matter.) The ratio is scale-invariant, so this holds at n=200000 too.

totals_eval.py.verdict: CORE INVARIANTS ARE REAL; THE GOVERNANCE LAYER AROUND THEM IS NOT. I reproduced the claimed mutation suite: all 23 rule-deletions I could construct from the claimed rule list turn the selftest red, so the structural gate (8/19 push mass, line binding, partition, integer/grid/positive-rate/cap domain), the Poisson deviance arithmetic, the banned-mean companions, the push convention in the calibration slope, and the whole/half separation are all genuinely load-bearing and correctly computed. But I ran 33 further adversarial mutations and 13 survived, and the survivors cluster in exactly the places the module makes its loudest claims. Three are serious: (1) the "hash-pinned, cannot be widened after the freeze" preregistration is defeated by the ordinary edit — 7 of 8 thresholds can be widened to nonsense and re-pinned in the same commit with the selftest still green, because PREREG_SHA lives in the file it pins; (2) the module's human-readable output raises TypeError on a window where every row is excluded for a missing final, which is the module's own flagship R1 case and, per this repo's git log ("8/21 slate incomplete, settlement deferred"), the real operating mode; (3) promotion_status reports THRESHOLDS_MET_AWAITING_OWNER_PROMOTION on a window where all eight non-empty-family subgroups and all ten calibration deciles are flagged UNDERPOWERED, because it never consults underpowered_subgroups — the POWER rule is enforced in the report and ignored by the gate that matters. Beyond those, banned_mean_gate is keyed on the literal string "mae" and therefore does not enforce two of the four things it is claimed to enforce; push_mass_block() is a whole report block with zero test coverage (it can be made to return garbage, or to report half_line_expected_pushes = 99.0 in flat contradiction of the invariant string printed next to it, with the selftest green); priced rows can vanish from all ten calibration deciles with no accounting; and an absurd model_total ships mae=1e+308 and mean_poisson_deviance=Infinity as numbers past a report gate that says "passed": true, emitting non-RFC-8259 JSON. No look-ahead exists inside the module (it is genuinely pure, no I/O, no import-time chdir — the unified_card os.chdir it cites is real at unified_card.py:19), but there is also no mechanism that could detect look-ahead in its input: `date` is read at line 164 for a label and discarded, no as-of/vintage field exists, and rows are not deduplicated, so 10 games submitted 12 times satisfies both n>=100 thresholds. The threshold freeze protects the half of the comparison nobody was going to game; the sample is entirely caller-controlled and unaudited.

defects.issue: The preregistration hash pin does not survive the one edit it exists to stop. PREREG_SHA (line 95) is stored in the same file as PREREG_THRESHOLDS (lines 79-90), and the only integrity check is the selftest's `_prereg_sha(PREREG_THRESHOLDS) != PREREG_SHA`, which any re-pin satisfies by construction. Widening a threshold and recomputing the constant in the same edit reads as clean: prereg_tampered=False, status is not PREREG_TAMPERED. The claimed rule 'any post-hoc edit reads as PREREG_TAMPERED and no threshold may then read as met' is only true for a *runtime* override passed as the `prereg=` argument, which is the one attack nobody performs.

Widened one threshold and recomputed the pin in the same edit, then ran the selftest:

  max_mae                     2.50 -> 99.0   GREEN -- NOT CAUGHT
  max_median_ae               2.00 -> 99.0   GREEN -- NOT CAUGHT
  max_abs_signed_bias         0.35 -> 99.0   RED (caught)
  max_mean_poisson_deviance   1.35 -> 99.0   GREEN -- NOT CAUGHT

  calibration_slope_max       1.20 -> 99.0   GREEN -- NOT CAUGHT
7 of 8 pass silently. max_abs_signed_bias is caught only by accident: an unrelated value fixture (the +0.72 hot-window test at selftest section 11) happens to assert that specific number. On the re-pinned file the 8/21 read returns status=DIAGNOSTIC, prereg_tampered=False, and abs_signed_bias now reports as MET: 'abs_signed_bias: 0.72 vs |bias| <= 1.0'.
defects.fix: Move the pin out of the pinned file: read the expected sha from a separate committed artifact (or the git object of a frozen JSON file), and have the selftest assert the *literal threshold values* one by one — the way max_abs_signed_bias is accidentally protected today — so a re-pin cannot be self-consistent. But the module does not deliver what its docstring claims. Three defects are disqualifying as-is: (1) the freeze covers only the five levellers, so deleting the underpowered withholding or redefining Brier as absolute error still SCORES against an untouched frozen spec and prints 'acc 0.0000 ... ABOVE_REPORTING_FLOOR' for the 0-4 cell; (2) there is no look-ahead control whatsoever — frozen_at_utc is caller-supplied, unvalidated ('banana' scores and is printed as provenance), never compared to anything, and rows carry no date, while the axes were demonstrably chosen from the 8/21 results they will be used to score; (3) the --json surface publishes accuracy 0.0 / brier 0.30435 for the n=4 cell with rate_null_reason null, so the withholding is only a rendering choice. freshness_gates.py.verdict: The six gates are real and the fixture suite is overwhelmingly load-bearing — all 6 whole-gate deletions and 41 of 45 behaviour-changing sub-rule mutations turn the selftest red (run out-of-tree in /tmp; the original was never edited). The boundary arithmetic is exact (21 passes / 22 fires / 30 fires naming both numbers, `>` not `>=`), outcome-blindness is genuine (an outcome-aware escape hatch is killed), and additivity, frozen ordering, index alignment, fail-loud, immutability, determinism and the leak sweep all resist mutation. There is no Brier/log-loss/deviance/calibration arithmetic in this module, so that check is N/A. BUT the module does not hold the doctrine it advertises. Three independent "row self-certifies past its own gate" holes exist, and every one of them is unclaimed and untested: (1) a precomputed `feature_state_age_days` short-circuits the date arithmetic and is never reconciled with the `feature_state_as_of`/`slate_date` sitting in the same row — the headline live case (2026-07-22 freeze on the 8/21 slate) clears the gate outright if the row says `staleness_days: 0`, and a NEGATIVE precomputed age (a state dated after the slate = the look-ahead case R1 claims to catch) passes silently; (2) `venue.neutral_site_modeled: True` on the gated row disables gate 3, directly contradicting gate 5's own "a row's own claim cannot override" doctrine; (3) `prices: {"markets": {}}` and a top-level `cross_book/basis` beside a `markets` map bypass gate 6 entirely. Worst in consequence: partial per-side book attribution (`{"book":"dk","book_home":"fd","ml_away":-118,"ml_home":102}`) passes gate 6, and daily_baselines.devig_entry then de-vigs that very pair to p_home=0.4777 — a NUMBER returned where the 8/3 ruling demands null-with-reason, from a pair whose two sides are labelled to different books. Claimed rule 7's "shapes mirror daily_baselines.devig_entry so a pair this gate passes is one that module can legitimately de-vig" is false in both directions. Finally, "UNKNOWN IS NOT CLEAN (R1)" is applied by only one of the six gates: deleting the `venue`, `starters`, or (outside wnba) `feature_state_as_of` key silently clears the corresponding gate, and the returned {"blocked": False, "statuses": []} cannot distinguish "six gates checked and clean" from "three gates had nothing to check" — the exact diagnostic-read-as-clearance failure. No caller exists yet (grep for freshness_gates/evaluate_gates outside the file returns nothing), so these are contract defects ahead of wiring, not live losses.

defects.issue: The one object returns three different answers to one question, and all eight identities pass on every such row. This is the class of contradiction the record claims to have made impossible.
defects.evidence: WNBA games cannot tie, so home -0.5, pick'em and home +0.5 are the identical bet (home must win outright). The frozen cell rule assigns them cover_continuous(-0.5)=P(M>0.5), P(M>0), and cover_continuous(+0.5)=P(M>-0.5). At sigma 13.97: mu=0 -> 0.485725 / 0.500000 / 0.514275 (spread 2.855pp); mu=-4.08 (the GSV@CHI value) -> 0.371514 / 0.385123 / 0.398874 (2.736pp); mu=+3.55 -> 0.586412 / 0.600297 / 0.614056 (2.764pp). assert_identities passes I1-I8 on all of them (/tmp/coh, section A). The cause: the continuity correction is applied at every line except the three straddling zero, because s=0 is an integer line that the record routes to the half-point branch by fiat ('at s = 0 no cell is applied'). Consequence: the ~2.86pp of mass in the impossible band |M| < 0.5 is never removed, and it lands on home cover for s >= 0 and away cover for s < 0 — verified at s=+1, cover 0.5142755 vs lattice-correct P(M>=1)=0.4857245. Worse, I1 is purchased by that choice: apply the correction consistently and p_home crosses 0.500 at mu = 0.5, not mu = 0, so the sign identity is a consequence of a modelling choice that biases the win probability, not the family-independent theorem about medians the record presents it as. 2.86pp is over half the 5pp band the record calls 'licensed disagreement'.
defects.fix: Choose one representation and apply it everywhere. Either (a) drop the lattice/continuity correction entirely, price every line off the continuous law (cover(s)=P(M>-s), push=0 at all lines), and accept that integer-line push probability is not modelled; or (b) apply the correction consistently, define p_home := P(M >= 1) = cover_continuous(-0.5), and restate I1 as p_home > 0.5 <=> m > 0.5 — which is honest but destroys the sign identity as currently marketed. defects.evidence: G2: 'date-block bootstrap resampling SLATE DATES with replacement, 10000 draws, seed 20260822, on paired per-date mean score differences; 95% CI must exclude zero on the improving side.' G6: 'Holm across the family {...} = 4 tests.' No bridge between the two is specified.
defects.fix: Preregister the bridge: bootstrap p-value as 2*min(P(d>=0), P(d<=0)) over the 10000 draws, Holm at family alpha 0.05 across the 4 tests, CI reported descriptively alongside. Or drop Holm and state the CI rule for all four comparisons with an explicitly widened level.

defects.issue: F7 is worded as a previous-slate condition but is populated with the game's own realized error, a post-outcome quantity that cannot exist on a pregame decision surface. As written it asks the gate to read a look-ahead field.

The record's own evidence block gives IND@DAL error +0.5 and ATL@LAS error -36.1 as errors from the SAME slate (2026-08-20), each on its own game - not from a previous slate.
defects.fix: Either re-word to 'a WNBA row on a slate following a 0.5-error night' with the prior-slate grade as the input, or drop the error framing and give R-A6 a fixture that sets an explicit override flag, which is the only shape a gate can actually refuse.

defects.issue: G1's '>= 60 distinct slate dates' floor never binds and is therefore not a second constraint. At the record's own stated 2.6 games per WNBA slate date, 200 games requires roughly 77 dates, so the game count dominates the date count everywhere in the reachable region.
defects.evidence: Record: '>= 200 prospective WNBA games across >= 60 distinct slate dates' and 'at roughly 2.6 games per WNBA slate date, 200 games over 60 dates is not reachable'. 60 dates * 2.6 = 156 games < 200; 200 games / 2.6 = 77 dates > 60.
defects.fix: Either raise the date floor so it binds (>= 77, or a per-season minimum so the sample provably spans seasons), or state plainly that the date floor is a redundant guard and the game count is the operative gate.
